title: Global Climate Summit Ends Without Final Agreement
subtitle: Deep disagreements over fossil fuels and money for developing nations lead to a historic breakdown in talks.

summary.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially ended without a final agreement. Negotiations lasted longer than any previous climate conference in history. A group of countries led by the European Union rejected the final proposal because it did not mention moving away from fossil fuels. Developing nations also expressed frustration over a lack of financial support for climate disasters. The failure to reach a deal means that major decisions will be delayed until next year.
summary.zh: 在土耳其舉行的 COP31 氣候峰會已正式結束，但未能達成最終協議。此次談判時間創下歷史新高。以歐盟為首的一群國家因最終提案未提及擺脫化石燃料而予以否決。開發中國家也對氣候災難缺乏財務支持表達不滿。未能達成協議意味著重大決策將延至明年處理。

paragraphs.en: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, has officially ended without a final agreement. After two weeks of intense negotiations and two extra days of overtime, the conference concluded on Sunday in a state of disagreement. This event is now officially the longest-running climate summit in history, yet it failed to produce the consensus required by the United Nations to move forward on global climate action.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其安塔利亞（Antalya）舉行的第 31 屆聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）已正式結束，但未能達成最終協議。經過兩週激烈的談判以及兩天的延長賽，會議於週日在一片分歧中落幕。這場會議已成為史上耗時最長的氣候峰會，卻未能產出聯合國推動全球氣候行動所需的共識。

paragraphs.en: The main point of conflict was a proposed document known as the Antalya Pact. Many countries, led by the European Union, refused to support this text. According to Deutsche Welle, the EU and other nations, including the UK, Panama, and the Marshall Islands, rejected the deal because it did not include a clear commitment to move away from coal, oil, and gas. Irish climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU, stated that they would not accept a decision that failed to mention fossil fuels, which are the primary cause of climate change.
paragraphs.zh: 衝突的核心在於一份名為「安塔利亞公約」的草案。以歐盟為首的多個國家拒絕支持該文本。根據德國之聲（Deutsche Welle）報導，歐盟及包括英國、巴拿馬與馬紹爾群島在內的其他國家，因該協議未包含明確承諾以擺脫煤炭、石油與天然氣而予以否決。代表歐盟發言的愛爾蘭氣候部長達拉·歐布萊恩（Darragh O'Brien）表示，他們無法接受一份未提及化石燃料的決議，因為化石燃料正是氣候變遷的主因。

paragraphs.en: This disagreement followed a controversial change to the draft text. Earlier in the week, a version of the agreement had included language about ending the use of fossil fuels. However, a later version removed these mentions entirely. This change caused significant anger among many delegates. While the COP31 presidency, led by Turkey and Australia, hoped the final text would bridge the gap between nations, the effort was not enough to satisfy the majority of the participants.
paragraphs.zh: 這場分歧源於草案內容的一項爭議性變動。在本週稍早，協議版本中曾包含關於終止使用化石燃料的措辭，然而後續版本卻將這些內容完全刪除。此舉引發許多與會代表強烈不滿。儘管由土耳其與澳洲主導的 COP31 主席團希望最終文本能彌合各國分歧，但這些努力仍不足以滿足大多數參與者。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the debate over fossil fuels, there was also a major dispute regarding climate finance. Developing countries, which are often the most affected by climate-related disasters like floods and heatwaves, argued that wealthy nations were not providing enough support. According to Deutsche Welle, these nations criticized the EU and other rich countries for demanding higher climate goals while refusing to provide the necessary money to help poorer countries adapt to a changing environment. Harjeet Singh, an activist with the Fill the Fund campaign, noted that it is unfair to ask developing nations to change their economies while they are struggling with debt and climate disasters.
paragraphs.zh: 除了化石燃料的爭論外，氣候融資問題也引發了重大糾紛。開發中國家往往是洪水與熱浪等氣候災難受害最深的地區，他們主張富裕國家提供的支持嚴重不足。根據德國之聲報導，這些國家批評歐盟及其他富國，一方面要求更高的氣候目標，另一方面卻拒絕提供必要的資金，以協助貧窮國家適應變遷中的環境。參與「填補基金」（Fill the Fund）運動的倡議人士哈吉特·辛格（Harjeet Singh）指出，要求正受困於債務與氣候災難的開發中國家改變其經濟結構，是不公平的。

paragraphs.en: Not all countries shared the same view. Russia, for example, supported the decision to leave out specific language about phasing out fossil fuels, arguing that countries should be able to decide their own energy paths. Meanwhile, some nations like Pakistan and Ghana suggested that the agreement was a necessary compromise, urging delegates to build bridges rather than barriers. Despite these efforts, the lack of a clear path forward on both energy and funding led to the eventual collapse of the talks.
paragraphs.zh: 並非所有國家都持相同觀點。例如，俄羅斯支持刪除關於逐步淘汰化石燃料的具體措辭，主張各國應有權決定自身的能源路徑。同時，巴基斯坦與迦納等國則認為該協議是必要的妥協，敦促代表們建立橋樑而非築起高牆。儘管有這些努力，但在能源與資金問題上缺乏明確的前進方向，最終導致談判破局。

paragraphs.en: This is only the second time in the history of UN climate meetings, which began in 1995, that countries have failed to reach a final agreement. The failure to secure a deal means that many critical decisions, including targets for climate finance, have been pushed to future meetings. UN climate chief Simon Stiell admitted that the summit fell short of its goals. However, he and other leaders emphasized that the process remains the primary way for the world to address the climate crisis together.
paragraphs.zh: 這是自 1995 年聯合國氣候會議召開以來，歷史上第二次未能達成最終協議。無法達成協議意味著包括氣候融資目標在內的許多關鍵決策，都將推遲至未來的會議處理。聯合國氣候變遷綱要公約執行秘書西蒙·斯蒂爾（Simon Stiell）坦言，此次峰會未達預期目標。然而，他與其他領袖強調，此機制仍是全球共同應對氣候危機的主要途徑。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the focus now shifts to next year's summit in Ethiopia. The Ethiopian delegate stated that the world needs to remember that working together requires determination, especially during difficult times. While the outcome in Antalya was disappointing for many, there is still a strong hope that future meetings will provide the necessary progress. For now, the world remains without a new global plan, leaving many questions about how countries will work together to keep global temperature increases below the 1.5C limit set by the 2015 Paris Agreement.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，焦點已轉向明年在衣索比亞舉行的峰會。衣索比亞代表表示，世界必須銘記，團結合作需要決心，尤其是在艱難時刻。雖然安塔利亞的結果令許多人感到失望，但各界仍強烈期盼未來的會議能取得必要進展。目前，全球仍缺乏新的國際計畫，這也讓各國如何攜手合作，以達成 2015 年《巴黎協定》所設定將全球升溫控制在攝氏 1.5 度以內的目標，留下了許多疑問。

paragraphs.en: The UK government also faced criticism during the summit regarding its own energy policies. While the UK pushed for stronger language on moving away from fossil fuels, some observers pointed out that the country is still considering new oil and gas projects in the North Sea. Critics argued that this creates a contradiction in the UK's position as a climate leader. As the dust settles on the Antalya summit, the pressure remains on all nations to reconcile their domestic energy needs with the urgent global requirement to reduce carbon emissions.
paragraphs.zh: 英國政府在峰會期間也因其自身的能源政策面臨批評。儘管英國力推更強硬的措辭以擺脫化石燃料，但部分觀察家指出，該國仍在考慮於北海進行新的油氣開發計畫。批評者認為，這使得英國作為氣候領袖的立場產生矛盾。隨著安塔利亞峰會塵埃落定，各國仍面臨巨大壓力，必須在國內能源需求與全球迫切的減碳要求之間取得平衡。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To reduce the differences between two groups or ideas to make them closer.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述物理上的橋樑，這裡比喻解決意見不合。文中：While the COP31 presidency, led by Turkey and Australia, hoped the final text would bridge the gap between nations, the effort was not enough to satisfy the majority of the participants.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To fail to reach a standard or goal.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思容易誤解為「掉落」，這裡指表現不如預期。文中：UN climate chief Simon Stiell admitted that the summit fell short of its goals.

keyTerms.definitionEn: When a situation becomes calmer after a period of excitement or confusion.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常用於比喻事件結束後的平靜狀態。文中：As the dust settles on the Antalya summit, the pressure remains on all nations to reconcile their domestic energy needs with the urgent global requirement to reduce carbon emissions.

This move has angered many countries and environmental campaigners who fear the event will fail to produce meaningful results. Panama has threatened to block the final outcome unless their demands are met. The summit is now facing pressure to restore stronger climate commitments before it ends.

previousArticles.summaryEn: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has entered overtime as nearly 200 countries fail to reach a final agreement. A major point of conflict is the removal of fossil fuel references from the latest draft deal. Developing nations and activists have expressed deep frustration with the slow progress and lack of ambition. Meanwhile, a separate dispute over the timing of future climate science reports is threatening to delay global action. Negotiators are now working through the weekend in hopes of finding common ground.

quiz.question: What was the primary reason the European Union and several other nations refused to sign the Antalya Pact?

options.A: They disagreed with the financial contributions requested from developing countries.
options.B: The final draft lacked a specific commitment to phase out fossil fuels.
options.C: They were dissatisfied with the leadership provided by Turkey and Australia.
options.D: The summit lasted longer than expected, causing logistical issues for delegates.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，歐盟及其他國家拒絕該協議，是因為該文本未包含明確承諾來擺脫煤炭、石油和天然氣。選項 A 錯誤，因為關於氣候資金的爭議是開發中國家提出的，而非歐盟拒簽的主因。選項 C 雖提到土耳其與澳洲的領導，但文中並未將此列為歐盟拒簽的理由。選項 D 雖然提到會議超時，但這並非導致拒簽的實質內容原因。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might the UK's position at the summit be considered hypocritical by some observers?

options.A: Because the UK was one of the countries that ultimately blocked the final agreement.
options.B: Because the UK demanded financial support from developing nations while refusing to pay its own share.
options.C: Because the UK advocated for ending fossil fuel use while simultaneously planning new domestic extraction projects.
options.D: Because the UK supported Russia's view that countries should determine their own energy paths.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章最後一段，雖然英國在峰會上推動更強硬的去化石燃料措辭，但觀察家指出英國國內仍在考慮北海的新油氣項目，這與其氣候領導者的立場產生矛盾。選項 A 錯誤，因為英國是反對該協議缺乏去化石燃料承諾的國家之一，而非阻撓協議簽署的國家。選項 B 與 D 均與文章事實不符，英國並未要求開發中國家資助，也未支持俄羅斯的立場。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'as the dust settles' mean in the context of the summit?

options.A: As the physical cleaning of the conference hall begins.
options.B: As the situation becomes clearer after the initial chaos or excitement.
options.C: As the delegates prepare to travel back to their home countries.
options.D: As the environmental damage from the summit is being measured.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。片語 'as the dust settles' 在此處為比喻用法，意指在混亂、激烈的爭論或重大事件結束後，局勢逐漸平靜並變得清晰，人們開始反思結果。選項 A 是字面意思的誤解，與會議內容無關。選項 C 與 D 雖然是會議結束後會發生的事，但該片語強調的是對事件影響的評估與沉澱，而非單純的交通或清潔過程。

quiz.question: What is the central theme regarding the outcome of the COP31 climate summit?

options.A: The summit was a total success because it set a new record for the longest-running climate negotiation.
options.B: The summit failed because wealthy nations refused to participate in any climate discussions.
options.C: The summit highlighted deep global divisions over fossil fuel policies and climate finance, resulting in no final agreement.
options.D: The summit proved that the United Nations is no longer an effective platform for addressing climate change.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體描述了 COP31 因化石燃料議題與氣候資金分配問題，導致各國無法達成共識，最終未能簽署協議。選項 A 將會議長度視為成功是不正確的，文中明確指出這是一次失敗。選項 B 錯誤，因為富國有參與，只是在資金與能源立場上與開發中國家有衝突。選項 D 過度推論，文中最後提到聯合國官員仍強調該機制是解決氣候危機的主要途徑。
